label: Experimental Facts
notes: Welcome the class to Arnold's opening chapter, where mechanics is built from three experimental pillars rather than axioms handed down. Stress that relativity, determinacy, and Galilean symmetry are claims about the world that experiments confirm, and that the whole formal apparatus of later chapters grows out of these few honest observations.

label: Galilean Space-Time
notes: Define the affine four-dimensional arena before any group acts on it. Emphasize that absolute time gives a well-defined notion of simultaneity and of time intervals, while space carries a Euclidean metric only within each instant. Warn students that there is no canonical way to identify points of space at different times until an observer is chosen.

label: The Principle of Relativity
notes: State Galileo's principle plainly: the laws of motion are identical in every inertial frame, so no mechanical experiment performed inside a closed cabin reveals uniform motion. Contrast this with acceleration, which is detectable. This single experimental fact is what forces the transformation group and constrains every admissible force law later in the chapter.

label: The Galilean Group
notes: Walk through the generators one at a time: time translation, space translation, rotation, and the boost to a uniformly moving frame. Count the ten parameters and note that composing any two such maps gives another, so they form a group. Reassure students this is exactly the symmetry that the relativity principle demands of mechanics.

label: The Galilean Boost
notes: Focus on the boost, the most distinctive Galilean transformation. Draw the two frames and show how a point's position picks up the term v times t while time itself is untouched. Highlight that velocities add by simple vector addition and that simultaneity is preserved, the feature that classical mechanics later trades away in relativity.

label: Newton's Principle of Determinacy
notes: Present determinacy as the deepest experimental input: the present positions and velocities of all points fix the entire future and past motion. Make clear this is why second-order equations appear, since exactly two pieces of initial data per coordinate are needed. Frame acceleration as the quantity nature is allowed to prescribe as a function of state.

label: Configuration Space
notes: Introduce configuration space as the manifold of all instantaneous positions, with dimension equal to the number of degrees of freedom. Explain that a motion is a curve in this space and that velocity is its tangent vector. Stress that the true state lives one level up, in position together with velocity, which is what determinacy actually specifies.

label: Newton's Equation
notes: Write Newton's equation as the concrete form that determinacy takes: acceleration equals a force function of position, velocity, and time. Emphasize that the function on the right is determined experimentally for each system, and that existence and uniqueness of solutions is exactly the mathematical echo of the physical principle of determinacy.

label: State Determines Trajectory
notes: Use the phase picture to make determinism visual. A single point of the position-velocity plane launches exactly one trajectory, and distinct trajectories never cross there. Contrast this with the configuration line, where curves may cross because the same position can carry different velocities. This is the intuition behind the existence and uniqueness theorem.

label: Galilean Invariance Constrains Force
notes: Now harvest consequences. Demand that Newton's equation look identical in every Galilean frame and watch the force law lose freedom. Time-translation invariance forbids explicit time dependence in a closed system, space-translation invariance forces dependence on differences of positions, and rotational invariance forbids any preferred direction.

label: Two-Body Forces
notes: Specialize to two interacting particles. Galilean symmetry plus the action-reaction balance forces the interaction to lie along the line joining them and to depend only on their separation distance. Newtonian gravity and the Coulomb law are the famous instances. Point out how much physics follows from symmetry alone, before any specific dynamics is assumed.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Recap the logical chain: relativity gives the Galilean group, determinacy gives second-order equations, and invariance carves the admissible forces. Preview that the next chapters lift this into the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian pictures, where these same symmetries reappear as conservation laws through Noether's theorem. Invite questions on any link in the chain.
